rule_summary: DCJ accepts foster care applications from anyone over 18.
notes: Applies to carers authorised by the Department of Communities and Justice (DCJ). Accredited non-government agencies can set their own minimum; see au-nsw-min_age-2.

rule_summary: Barnardos requires its foster carers to be at least 25, with exceptions for kinship carers.
notes: Agency rule for Barnardos Australia (NSW and ACT), not a state rule.

rule_summary: DCJ states there is no upper age limit for fostering with DCJ.
Singles, people who are dating and couples may apply, including LGBTQIA+ people. A new partner must go through background checks.
Applicants need to be financially stable, enough to meet their own needs and commitments.
notes: The same page says applicants may work full time, part time, casually or not at all.

rule_summary: Applicants may rent or own their home.
No spare bedroom is required. The child needs adequate space for a bed or cot and furniture, and privacy suited to their age.
notes: Wording on the page: 'Do I need to own my home and do I need a spare bedroom?'.

rule_summary: The number of children a carer may care for is set as a condition of each carer's authorisation.
notes: From a search engine extract of a DCJ page for service providers; the page text read by the project's reader stopped before this section. No statewide maximum was found.

rule_summary: Carers and co-residents aged 18 and over need a Working with Children Check. Police and national criminal record checks cover everyone aged 16 and over.
notes: A co-resident stays 21 or more nights a year on the property. DCJ also checks its child protection records for those 16 and over, and interstate or New Zealand records where relevant.

rule_summary: Before authorisation an agency must complete probity checks, including Working with Children Check, national police, Community Services and other agency checks.
legal_citation: Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Regulation 2022 (NSW), s 18 and sch 2 cl 2
notes: Citation as given by the Office of the Children's Guardian; regulation text not read (legislation.nsw.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader). Fact sheet dated November 2025. The December 2025 OCG fact sheet on checks says household members aged 16 and over need a National Police Check.

rule_summary: At least two references on the person's suitability are required, with a health statement and a medical report.
legal_citation: Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Regulation 2022 (NSW), sch 2 cl 2
notes: Unit 'other' means referees. Citation as given by the Office of the Children's Guardian; regulation text not read (legislation.nsw.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader).

rule_summary: A qualified assessor completes a carer assessment over several home visits. It includes two referees, two support people, the applicant's children and a home inspection.
notes: The DCJ page does not name the assessment tool. The applicant can review the report before authorisation and signs the Code of Conduct for Authorised Carers.

rule_summary: Shared Lives training is mandatory: four 3-hour sessions (12 hours), then 4 more hours of Part two during the assessment.
notes: The video on the same page says 16 hours of training.

rule_summary: Carer reviews look at the Carer Development Plan and identify training or support needs. No yearly hours are stated.
Carers are reviewed at the end of their first year, then usually every 12 months.
notes: Applies to carers authorised by DCJ or non-government agencies. A review can happen sooner if circumstances change.

rule_summary: Every five years DCJ carers complete a fuller authorisation review, with criminal record checks for household members 18 and over and a health review.
notes: The page says this applies to DCJ carers.

rule_summary: It can take up to six months from first enquiry to authorisation. The background check step can take up to three months.
notes: DCJ says it will call within two working days of an online enquiry.

rule_summary: The DCJ standard care allowance for ages 0 to 4 is $697 a fortnight from 1 January 2026.
notes: nsw.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader for this page; read from a search engine extract. The extract says standard rates rose by 20 per cent on this date and that the carers FAQ gives $697.20. Carers with non-government agencies may receive different rates. Any indexation after 1 July 2026 not checked.

rule_summary: At least one adult applicant must be a citizen or permanent resident, or legally able to stay in Australia long-term. DCJ carers must live in NSW.
Applicants must be over 18 to be assessed as a carer.
notes: Page last updated 27 August 2026.

rule_summary: There is no upper age limit. Applicants complete a health form and Child Safety seeks a GP medical clearance.
Carers can be single, married, de facto or a same-sex couple.
A person living with a spouse may only hold a certificate of approval jointly with that spouse.
legal_citation: Child Protection Act 1999 (Qld), s 132(3)
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt).

rule_summary: Carers do not have to be wealthy or have a large home.
Carers do not have to own their home; renters can foster.
An empty room is not required. Children in care can share a room with the carer's own children if there is capacity.
No fixed number is stated. The number of children is agreed in the carer assessment and depends on more than house size.
Carers and every adult household member must hold a blue card or exemption card (Queensland's Working with Children Check).
legal_citation: Working with Children Check Act 2000 (Qld), sch 1 s 14 (as cited in the practice manual)
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt). Blue cards last 3 years. Changes to remove the blue card rule for kinship carers will not start until a new screening framework exists (Blue cards page).

rule_summary: Child Safety assesses the child protection, domestic violence and traffic history of applicants and adult household members.
legal_citation: Child Protection Act 1999 (Qld), s 135(1)
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt). Overseas checks can be requested where a person lived abroad for 6 months or more.

rule_summary: Assessment covers an application, interview, Household Safety Study and health questionnaire. The assessor's report addresses the standards of care.
legal_citation: Child Protection Act 1999 (Qld), s 135; Child Protection Regulation 2023 (Qld), ss 23, 24, 27
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt). Household Safety Study is the name used on qld.gov.au.

rule_summary: Foster carer applicants must complete training before approval, with competency assessed against learning outcomes.
legal_citation: Child Protection Regulation 2023 (Qld), ss 23, 24
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt). The course is called Getting Ready to Start (Next steps page). Hours not stated. Not required for kinship carers.

rule_summary: In their first 12 months, foster carers complete Starting Out modules, including the trauma-informed Hope and Healing course.
notes: After that, learning needs are recorded in the Foster Carer Agreement (Training page). No yearly hours are stated.

rule_summary: A new foster carer is first approved for 12 months.
notes: Kinship carers are approved for up to 12 months. Page last updated 16 April 2025.

rule_summary: Each renewal lasts 3 years. Carers must apply before the certificate expires, or the approval lapses.
notes: Kinship carer renewals are for up to 3 years. Renewal repeats the checks, interviews and Household Safety Study.

rule_summary: Applicants are asked to allow 3 months from the time they apply.
notes: Page last updated 17 September 2026.

rule_summary: Child Safety must decide an initial application within 90 days of it being properly made, unless the applicant agrees in writing to more time.
legal_citation: Child Protection Act 1999 (Qld), ss 143(1), 143A
notes: Citation as given in the Child Safety Practice Manual; legislation text not read (legislation.qld.gov.au disallows automated readers in robots.txt). If not decided in time, the application must be refused, which is a reviewable decision.

rule_summary: The fortnightly caring allowance for ages 0 to 5 is $652.40 from 1 January 2026.
notes: The 2025 rate was $623.00. Age bands are 0-5, 6-10 and 11 and over. A regional remote loading is paid on top in some areas.

rule_summary: Applicants do not need to be Australian citizens or permanent residents.
There are no education requirements to become a foster carer.
Applicants must be at least 21.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). Berry Street and VACCA pages state the same minimum.

rule_summary: Anglicare Victoria states there is no upper age limit. Health is assessed through a health check.
notes: Agency page dated 19 December 2023. Fostering Connections says carers can be 'young or old'.

rule_summary: Carers can be single or in a couple. A partner and other adults at home go through the same checks.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). The FAQ page says both partners go through accreditation and training together.

rule_summary: Carers can rent or own their home.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt).

rule_summary: Applicants need one spare bedroom. Some agencies accept applicants without one to care for babies, case by case.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt).

rule_summary: The applicant and all adults in the household complete a police check and a Working with Children Check.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). Referee checks are for the applicant only.

rule_summary: Accredited foster carers must hold a current Working with Children Check and complete Victorian police checks every year.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt).

rule_summary: The agency visits the home and works through the assessments. A report goes to an accreditation panel with at least one DFFH representative.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). Accredited carers then sign a code of conduct agreement.

rule_summary: DFFH provides Step by Step, a competency-based assessment resource, for foster care agencies assessing prospective foster carers.
notes: DFFH sites disallow automated readers in robots.txt; read from a search engine extract. A separate Step by Step Aboriginal assessment tool is listed for agencies.

rule_summary: Applicants complete 16 hours of training during the assessment.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt).

rule_summary: Anglicare Victoria applicants complete Shared Lives training, roughly 16 hours, online or face to face.
notes: Agency page. Shared Lives is the course name the agency uses.

rule_summary: Agencies provide ongoing training. Carer KaFÉ offers learning and development to accredited foster carers across Victoria.
notes: Better Health Channel page reviewed 12 June 2024. No yearly hours are stated.

rule_summary: The safety of the carer's home is monitored through home visits and formally reviewed every year.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). How long accreditation lasts is not stated on the pages read.

rule_summary: Becoming an accredited foster carer usually takes six to nine months.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). Value is the upper end of the stated range.

rule_summary: The level one care allowance for ages 0 to 7 is $473.66 a fortnight in the 2026/2027 rate table.
notes: DFFH sites disallow automated readers in robots.txt; read from a search engine extract. The extract gives level two for ages 0 to 7 as $500.02. Effective date not seen.

rule_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents. Others may be accredited for respite or emergency care; NZ Special Category Visa holders are eligible.
notes: Fostering Connections is the statewide recruitment service run jointly by Victorian foster care agencies; DFFH pages could not be read (robots.txt). The FAQ adds that others may be considered for longer-term care of a particular child.

rule_summary: Foster carers need to be 18. Age may affect which child is placed with them.
notes: Undated Department of Communities FAQ, file posted May 2024. The 2024 brochure says the same.

rule_summary: No upper age limit is stated. Age may affect which child is placed.
Foster carers can be single, partnered or married, with or without children. LGBTQIA+ applicants are welcome.
Applicants and their partners need to be financially stable. The subsidy covers the child's costs and is not income.
Renters can foster but must check the tenancy agreement with the landlord. The carer must own the property or be named on the tenancy.
notes: The FAQ says boarders, and households with Airbnb guests, cannot be considered.

rule_summary: A child in care may share with the carer's own children after careful thought. Carers cannot share a bedroom with a child in care, except a baby.
notes: The baby exception follows safe sleeping guidance: same room, not same bed, up to 6 to 12 months.

rule_summary: The number of children is decided through the assessment, based on capacity to meet each child's needs.
All adults living in the home need police and Department checks and a Working with Children Card.
notes: Brochure file posted February 2024. The FAQ says the Screening Unit searches criminal records across Australia and overseas where relevant, and longer-staying visitors need a Record Screening Check.

rule_summary: An assessor visits several times and looks at meeting the child's needs, safety, teamwork and culture. The report goes to an approval committee.
notes: The brochure names the Interim Approval Committee; the FAQ names the Foster Carer Assessment Panel. Approved carers receive a Certificate of Approval.

rule_summary: All new foster carer applicants must complete Preparation Training before any child is placed. The in-person course is 18 hours.
notes: Required since 2017. Six 3-hour modules; a self-paced online version is also offered. The 2024 FAQ and brochure give 19 hours. Page last updated 18 May 2026.

rule_summary: Carers are invited to ongoing training each year, offered by districts and the Learning and Development team.
notes: No yearly hours are stated.

rule_summary: All foster carers must undergo a review every year.
notes: How long approval lasts is not stated.

rule_summary: Becoming a carer takes about 4 months, or longer.
The basic fortnightly carer subsidy for ages 0 to 6 is $523.88. Mid-West and Goldfields add 10%; Kimberley and Pilbara add 20%.
notes: 'Who pays in WA?' guide, dated April 2026, file posted July 2026. It does not say whether the figures include the 10 per cent increase from 1 July 2026 (see au-wa-board_rate-2).

rule_summary: A 10 per cent subsidy increase for all foster and family carers took effect on 1 July 2026.
notes: Government media statement of 1 July 2026.

rule_summary: Carers must be citizens or permanent residents living permanently in WA. New Zealand Special Category visa (subclass 444) holders may apply.
notes: Page last updated 18 May 2026.

rule_summary: Foster carers are generally aged between 25 and 70.
notes: Stated as 'generally', not as a fixed limit. Page last updated 7 August 2026.

rule_summary: Foster carers are generally aged between 25 and 70.
notes: Stated as 'generally', not as a fixed limit.

rule_summary: Foster carers can be individuals or couples, including same-sex couples, with or without children.
notes: The whole household meets the assessment worker.

rule_summary: Foster carers do not have to be rich or have a big house.
Each approval must carry a condition on how many children the carer may care for. It weighs capacity, care history, supports and room in the home.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 (SA), s 72(4)
notes: DCP procedure V3.0, August 2025. No statewide maximum was found.

rule_summary: The carer, all adults living in the house and regular guests with ongoing unsupervised contact must hold a Working with Children Check.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 (SA)
notes: Section not given on the page. Checks are done by the DHS Screening Unit and last 5 years; young people at home can apply from 17 years and 5 months.

rule_summary: DCP child protection history checks, and interstate checks, cover applicants, household members and regular household guests.
notes: Carer Approval Requirements Matrix v2.2, August 2026 (marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive but published on the DCP site).

rule_summary: Two referee checks are required for foster carer approval.
notes: Unit 'other' means referees. Carer Approval Requirements Matrix v2.2, August 2026 (marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive but published on the DCP site).

rule_summary: Foster carer competencies are evidenced through a Step by Step or Winangay foster care assessment.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 (SA), s 72(3)
notes: Carer Approval Requirements Matrix v2.2, August 2026 (marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive but published on the DCP site). A house plan and home safety check are also required.

rule_summary: There are around six assessment sessions in the home, each about 2 hours.
notes: Unit 'other' means sessions. Some agencies train and assess at the same time.

rule_summary: Required training: Provide First Aid, Safe Environments: Through their eyes, and Shared Lives or orientation training.
notes: Carer Approval Requirements Matrix v2.2, August 2026 (marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive but published on the DCP site). Cultural awareness training is required to care for Aboriginal children, and Safe Infant Care to care for children under 2. Hours not stated.

rule_summary: Carer reviews must make relevant training available. A carer agreement sets out the carer's training and support plan.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 (SA), s 73
notes: No yearly hours are stated.

rule_summary: Approved carers are reviewed on an ongoing basis; the carer approval unit sets the next review two years ahead.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Safety) Act 2017 (SA), s 73
notes: The DCP steps page says reviews typically occur every two years. Carer agreements are reviewed at the same time.

rule_summary: Becoming a registered foster carer usually takes between 6 and 9 months.
notes: Value is the upper end of the range. The sa.gov.au steps page says around 6 months.

rule_summary: The term base rate for ages 0 to 4 is $524.60 a fortnight ($37.47 a night) from 1 July 2026.
notes: Age bands are 0-4, 5-12, 13-15, 16-17 and 18+. Loadings for special needs are extra.

rule_summary: Applicants for foster care approval must be Australian citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Carer Approval Requirements Matrix v2.2, August 2026 (marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive but published on the DCP site).

rule_summary: Foster carers generally need to be over 21 to begin fostering.
notes: Stated as 'generally'. The December 2024 handbook says the same.

rule_summary: No upper age limit is stated. Age and capacity are part of matching, and health issues lead to a medical review.
Single people and couples can foster. Married or de facto couples are asked to have been together at least two years.
notes: Both partners attend training and take part in the assessment.

rule_summary: Carers do not need to own their home but need safe, stable accommodation with space for a child.
A bedroom must be available. Children of the same age and gender may share; teenagers 13 and over need their own space.
notes: Children may not share rooms with adults. DECYP will not place children in a household with an infant or where a child is expected.

rule_summary: Carers must hold Working with Vulnerable People registration. It applies to anyone over 16 working in a regulated activity.
notes: Carers give proof of registration and renewal to the department (DECYP).

rule_summary: Providers check criminal, child protection, domestic violence and other history, including national police and child safety checks.
notes: Becoming a Foster Carer in Tasmania handbook, December 2024.

rule_summary: Providers interview the applicant and household using the Step by Step assessment, with a housing check, wellbeing questionnaire and reference checks.
notes: The handbook says Step by Step is used in most states and territories. Each provider runs its own assessment and selection process.

rule_summary: Training is compulsory. Several providers use Shared Stories, Shared Lives, nine modules usually over two days; some use their own course.
notes: Hours not stated. The FAQ suggests adult children living at home attend some or all of the training.

rule_summary: Volunteers aged 18 and over must complete safeguarding training and a 15-minute video each year.
notes: Stated on the foster and kinship carer training page (published 21 May 2026). The page does not say in so many words that this covers carers; DECYP describes carers as volunteers.

rule_summary: Ongoing provider support includes annual reviews.
notes: How long approval lasts is not stated.

rule_summary: Becoming an approved foster carer usually takes between four and six months.
notes: Value is the upper end of the range.

rule_summary: Foster and kinship carers are paid a fortnightly allowance towards the cost of care. The page does not publish the rate.
notes: No current figure found. The DECYP news page says the 2026-27 Budget adds $2 million a year to carer allowances.

rule_summary: Foster carers must be Australian citizens or permanent residents.
Barnardos requires foster carers to be at least 25.
notes: Agency rule for Barnardos Australia, one of three ACT providers. No territory-wide minimum was found; act.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader.

rule_summary: OzChild requires ACT foster carers to be over 21.
notes: Agency rule. The page builds its text with JavaScript, so the project's reader got almost none; read from a search engine extract.

rule_summary: Barnardos sets no upper age limit.
notes: Agency page for the ACT.

rule_summary: Barnardos accepts applications from people of any marital status, sexual orientation or family structure.
notes: Agency page for the ACT.

rule_summary: OzChild asks ACT foster carers to have a spare bedroom.
notes: Agency rule; read from a search engine extract.

rule_summary: With some exceptions, anyone seeking approval as a carer must hold Working with Vulnerable People registration.
legal_citation: Children and Young People Act 2008 (ACT); Working with Vulnerable People (Background Checking) Act 2011 (ACT)
notes: Stated in the preamble of the Children and Young People (Kinship and Foster Carers Risk Assessment) Guidelines 2023 (DI2023-202). Section of the Act not given there.

rule_summary: The director-general must consider suitability information for the applicant and for each other adult in the household.
legal_citation: Children and Young People Act 2008 (ACT), ss 514B, 514C
notes: As summarised in DI2023-202. The Act itself was not read (its PDF exceeded the reader's size limit).

rule_summary: The director-general must be satisfied the person is appropriate, considering suitability information, references or reports and any medical examination.
legal_citation: Children and Young People Act 2008 (ACT), ss 514B(1), 514C
notes: As summarised in DI2023-202.

rule_summary: Barnardos assessors hold six to eight in-depth interviews. A report then goes to the Carer Assessment and Linking Panel.
notes: Unit 'other' means interviews; value is the upper end of the range. Agency process.

rule_summary: Barnardos foster care training is three full days, covering the care system, therapeutic parenting and trauma.
notes: Agency course; hours not stated.

rule_summary: Carers with a long-term Approved Carer Authority have a risk assessment every 5 years. Carers must report relevant changes within 7 days.
legal_citation: Children and Young People (Kinship and Foster Carers Risk Assessment) Guidelines 2023 (ACT) (DI2023-202); Children and Young People Act 2008 (ACT), s 514F
notes: An extra review can happen if significant concerns are raised.

rule_summary: OzChild says ACT accreditation takes about 4 to 7 months.
notes: Agency statement; read from a search engine extract. Value is the upper end of the range.

rule_summary: The 2025-26 guide lists $336.77 a week for approved kinship and foster carers of children aged 0 to 4.
notes: act.gov.au returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader; read from a search engine extract. The extract cut off the subsidy name. The guide says rates are back dated to 1 July 2025 and paid fortnightly in arrears. A newer guide may exist.

rule_summary: A nomination for approval as an authorised carer may cover two or more individuals who live together.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), reg 4(1) note
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked.

rule_summary: An authorised carer must hold a clearance notice in force. Each person aged 15 or over living with them must be fit and proper.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), regs 2, 3(a), 3(e), 4(2)(d)
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked. The regulations call people 15 and over 'mature persons'; each must consent to police release of their criminal history.

rule_summary: Everyone 18 and over in the household needs an Ochre Card. Everyone 15 and over needs a police check.
notes: NT Government sites returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader; read from a search engine extract. The Ochre Card is the NT Working with Children Clearance.

rule_summary: A nomination must include a character reference from someone who has known the individual for at least 12 months.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), reg 4(2)(c)
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked.

rule_summary: The CEO decides whether a nominee is fit and proper, considering criminal history, experience caring for children, health and character references.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), regs 3(c), 5
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked. The Act lets the regulations provide for approval of carers (Care and Protection of Children Act 2007 (NT), s 78(3)).

rule_summary: Carer applicants attend induction training before approval.
notes: NT Government sites returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader; read from a search engine extract. Emergency and Authorised Carer Assessment and Approval Policy, version 1.04 of 6 February 2026, per the extract. Hours not stated.

rule_summary: Carers must attend training or information sessions as directed by the CEO.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), reg 13(j)
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked.

rule_summary: Carers must provide appropriate accommodation for the child. The regulations do not define it further.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), reg 13(c)
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked.

rule_summary: Approval as an authorised carer lasts 2 years from notice, or to an earlier date in the notice. It ends if the clearance notice ends.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), regs 6, 8(1)
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked.

rule_summary: Authorised carers' approval is reviewed within the first 12 months and every two years after that.
notes: NT Government sites returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader; read from a search engine extract. Policy version 1.04 of 6 February 2026, per the extract.

rule_summary: The regulations provide for two kinds of approval: authorised carers and emergency carers.
legal_citation: Care and Protection of Children (Placement Arrangement) Regulations 2010 (NT), Parts 2 and 3
notes: Version read is the regulations as in force at 1 September 2010; later amendments not checked. Emergency approval runs from placement to midnight 3 days later, or until a decision on a nomination as an authorised carer (reg 11).

rule_summary: All foster and kinship carers receive the same age-based carer payment. Rates rose 10 per cent from 1 July 2026, including CPI indexation.
notes: NT Government sites returned HTTP 403 to the project's reader; read from a search engine extract. The 0-5 figure was not visible in the extract. The Act lets the CEO pay carers under the placement arrangement (Care and Protection of Children Act 2007 (NT), s 82).
